thesis: Pebblebrook (held) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-29 after the close: adjusted FFO of $0.63 per share, $0.11 above the high end of its own outlook, same-property hotel EBITDA of $115.2M (+15.1% YoY), full-year adjusted FFO guidance of $1.88-$1.92, and net debt to EBITDA down to 5.1x. This resolves the prior thesis's pending-print risk in its favor. The stock still slipped about 0.9% today to 21.53, 1.7% below its 52-week high (21.90). Strongest counter-case: the company still reports a GAAP net loss ($54.6M in Q3), a structural weakness named in the prior thesis that this run's results do not resolve, and leverage of 5.1x remains meaningful; the beat may also be largely priced in after a ~20% 60-day run. The search did not exhaustively check for scheduled litigation, restatements or equity raises, and none surfaced.
invalidation: Guidance is cut, RevPAR growth reverses, or leverage rises

thesis: RingCentral (held) is up about 20% over 60 calendar days (69.62 to 83.70) and closed at 81.37 today, 17% below its 52-week high of 98.14 (2026-10-23). Reports say it posted Q3 results on 2026-10-22 that beat expectations and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance (to roughly $5.07-$5.12), with analysts raising targets on AI adoption. This run found only aggregator-level coverage with conflicting prices and dates, so the catalyst is not verified against a primary filing. Strongest counter-case: the CFO stock sale disclosed in August 2026 and analyst targets that lagged the price, both named in the prior thesis and not resolved by any new dated fact, plus a soft revenue outlook amid AI competition. The price has retreated from its post-earnings high, which suggests profit-taking. No scheduled litigation, restatement or equity raise surfaced.
invalidation: Guidance walked back, AI revenue growth stalls, or price loses the post-earnings gap

thesis: Etsy is up about 12.6% over 60 calendar days (81.33 to a 91.59 close) after reporting Q3 2026 on 2026-10-28: revenue up 10.9% to about $692.5M against roughly $668M expected, adjusted EPS of $1.00 against about $0.76, adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.4%, and active buyers back to roughly 1% annual growth for the first time in two years. The stock hit a multi-year high of 94.49 on 2026-10-28 and fell about 2.9% to 88.96 today. Strongest counter-case: Q4 gross merchandise sales guidance of $3.46-3.52B implies only 5-7% growth, a slowdown from Q3's 8.8%, buyer growth is barely positive, and the CFO plans to step down in March 2027. This run did not resolve whether the slowdown outweighs the beat, so conviction is capped at medium. No scheduled litigation, restatement or equity raise surfaced, though the search was not exhaustive.
invalidation: Q4 guidance proves too high, buyer growth turns negative again, or margin expansion reverses
